The Maison · Est. 2016

The Atelier

Maison Velár is a Lagos-born house of couture, founded on a single conviction — that the highest luxury is the trace of a human hand.

Our Beginning

From a surulere workshop to the Paris runways.

Founder and creative director Adaeze Onuoha trained at the École de la Chambre Syndicale de la Couture Parisienne before returning home to Lagos in 2016. She opened a four-person workshop in Surulere with a single sewing machine inherited from her grandmother.

A decade later, Velár dresses women across three continents — yet every garment still passes through human hands, never an assembly line.

Our Craft

Heritage textiles, reimagined.

We work hand-in-hand with indigo dyers in Abeokuta and aso-oke weavers in Iseyin, reinterpreting centuries-old Yoruba techniques within the discipline of French couture.

A single Solstice gown carries 38 metres of hand-pleated silk, 11,000 glass beads, and roughly 240 hours of meticulous handwork.

Materials & Provenance
Silk

Mikado, crepe and organza, sourced from a century-old Como mill and pre-shrunk in-house.

Adire

Hand-dyed indigo resist cloth, produced with our long-standing dyers' collective in Abeokuta.

Aso-Oke

Hand-woven cotton and metallic thread from master weavers in Iseyin, Oyo State.

A Decade in Motion

The Velár timeline

2016

The first stitch

Velár opens in a Surulere workshop with four artisans and one inherited machine.

2018

Lagos Fashion Week

Debut runway collection “Irummobo” earns the Emerging Designer honour.

2021

The Paris showroom

A permanent showroom opens on Rue de Marignan, 8th arrondissement.

2023

Haute Couture

Velár presents its first full couture collection at Paris Couture Week.

2026

Solstice

The SS26 collection and a new 600m² Victoria Island atelier — our home for the next decade.
